note: Tempdoc 805 §G.2 — degradation-consequence coherence. A surface that CLAIMS what a degradation did to search ("showing keyword results", "keyword-ranked results") must derive that claim from the ONE classifier `classifyConsequence` (state/readinessNotice.ts) and word it from that module's exported caveat constants — never re-derive it from `verdict.severity` and re-author the wording locally. That re-derivation is the fork-class round 11 measured in TWO copies at once: the search banner and `availability.ts`'s affordance caveat both claimed a keyword fallback while the build's own search trace showed dense retrieval AND the cross-encoder executing (the true state was a PASSAGE-leg gap only). This gate (scripts/ci/check-consequence-classification.mjs) enforces both halves: (a) CLAIM CONTAINMENT — the keyword-fallback claim phrases appear in no file under `scanRoot` except the authority module, with a narrow allowlist for the trace-outcome line (searchTraceExplain describes the TRACE's own recorded outcome, not a derived claim) and for test files (which assert the claim's presence/absence); (b) POSITIVE COVERAGE — every registered consumer surface imports the classifier or the caveat constants, so a registered consumer cannot silently drop back to a private derivation. Honest limit (like capability-availability / verdict-derivation): the coverage half guards the REGISTERED consumers' seam, not a brand-new unregistered claim surface (that is a discovery-step register row); the containment half is literal-phrase matching, so a semantically-equivalent re-wording ("only word matches") passes — free-text wording judgment stays prose-tier.

allow.whyFiles: searchTraceExplain's `TIMEOUT: 'AI expansion timed out — keyword results only'` reports the TRACE's own recorded outcome for a stage that actually happened — it is a reading of measured execution, not a claim derived from reason codes, so it is not the fork-class this gate closes.
allow.whyTestFiles: `*.test.ts` files assert the claim's presence on the impairing branch and its ABSENCE on the passage/AI branches — the precision tests are the reason the phrase must appear in them.

whyConsumers: Tempdoc 837 §1.5 (UR-4) added verdict.ts: `verdictBody`'s degraded arm used to answer purely off `v.severity`, so a `warn` AI-only cause (inference.crashed) made the Health footer assert "Retrieval is degraded" while the banner — same verdict, same reason codes — correctly said search was fully working and only chat was off. That is the two-surfaces-one-verdict contradiction this register exists for, so the arm now consults `classifyConsequence` instead of re-deriving from severity.
